resourceSystem.name: Fate Links
resourceSystem.generationNote: Three tokens. A link reserves one token, except an authored covenant may reserve two; a link recovers only after it is closed and its uses are exhausted, returning its token at the start of the owning caster next own turn.

resourceGuide.tagline: Three threads, three links, and a public promise before the consequence.

vitals.label: Range
vitals.value: 30 ft formation each | 60 ft maintenance separation

vitals.label: Recovery
vitals.value: closed + exhausted | owning caster next own turn

gain.title: Reserve a Real Thread
gain.text: Tie the Thread reserves one of three tokens and records both endpoints, a public purpose, consent, one use and expiry. Tie and Cut are core grants.

hold.title: Keep the Promise Visible
hold.text: Every link names its source, target, public purpose, token state, remaining uses and absolute expiry. Distinct endpoints stay within 30 ft formation range each and 60 ft maintenance separation. At most three links and one consequence per link per round.

spend.title: Choose Who Bears the Risk
spend.text: A transfer moves at most three points of original assigned damage after mitigation from the protected actor to the chosen bearer. Ward, severance and re-anchoring use the same token record; none is a second bank.

risk.title: A Broken Link Has a Price
risk.text: Recovery begins only after the link is closed and its uses are exhausted. Its token then becomes recovering until the start of the owning caster next own turn. Cut links follow their own authored destination. No reconnect, initiative or scene-change refill; consent withdrawal ends the link immediately.

resourceGuide.exampleTurn: **Turn 1:** Reserve one token with Tie the Thread and record a public purpose. **Turn 2:** Use Shared Burden to redirect up to 2 original damage, then mark the use once. **Turn 3:** Cut the link with Cut Clean, or let it expire; once the link is closed and its uses are exhausted, the token returns at the start of the owning caster next own turn. No automatic AP, damage, expiry or recovery is applied.

weaveIn.text: Forty optional records and two core records; every price, consent term and expiry stays visible.
Covenant Weaver, Thread Cutter and Tapestry Keeper each have a signature and capstone with tree gates.
Fate Weaver has no registered native heritage edge. Kessen Neth access is not implied; the four acquisition requirements must be recorded.

quickStart.title: The First Thread
rows: One consented link, one use, expires at the end of the second subsequent caster turn
End one link; after closure and use exhaustion, its token returns at the owning caster next own turn
Redirect up to 2 original damage to you, once
Public purpose, consent, uses and expiry only
Sever one identified fate link; pay one recovering thread
quickStart.footnote: Read-only display: no token, link, AP, HP, movement, expiry or recovery is automatically applied.

resourceGuide.trackerHint: The integrated tracker starts uninitialized. It never invents a token, link, consent record, expiry or refill. Observer projections contain counts and public terms only.

extraSections.title: The Thread Ledger
extraSections.content: Record each link exactly once: both endpoints, public purpose, consent, token state, remaining uses and absolute expiry. Distinct endpoints stay within 30 ft formation range each and 60 ft maintenance separation. Three tokens and three links are hard caps. Recovery begins only after the link is closed and its uses are exhausted; the token then returns at the start of the owning caster next own turn. This is a manual tabletop record, not an automated combat authority.

materials: Three link cards naming both endpoints and the public purpose
A consent record and a use/expiry record
A next-own-turn recovery marker used only after closure and use exhaustion
